chunks: Saad narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydullah al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the sick person, does he make up the prayer if he loses consciousness? He said, 'No, except for the prayer during which he regained consciousness.'
ai.seo_question: Does a person who faints during prayer need to make it up later?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on the prayer of the compelled (*al-Mudtir*), this hadith clarifies the exemption from *qada* (making up) for prayers missed during unconsciousness, a key principle in Shia jurisprudence regarding *al-Jahd* (incapacity). The Imam specifies that if the patient regains consciousness within the prayer's time, they must perform that specific prayer, illustrating the nuanced application of ease (*rukhas*) in ritual worship. This ruling underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between temporary loss of capacity and permanent disability when determining religious obligations.
